question: Why did the principal mass-loss region of kerogen begin about 50 C later under air than under nitrogen?
expect: premise false: it began about 50 C EARLIER under air (abstract; sec. 3.1)
rendered: The principal mass-loss region of kerogen began approximately 50 °C earlier under air than under nitrogen, not later. This difference is particularly evident in Figure 4a, where the onset of the principal mass-loss region under air occurs approximately 50 °C earlier than under nitrogen.
